statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail is 20, at the bottom of the watch band, with NQ futures last verified at 29,235.50, down 213.25 points or 0.72%, sitting on a 29,216.75 Globex low that had been extended repeatedly from a 29,458.50 open. E-mini S&P 500 futures were likewise on their session low at 7,627.25. August PPI printed at 12:30 UTC with a hot 5.4% annual headline but a 0.2% monthly core against a 0.3% consensus, and initial claims came in at 206K against 205K expected, so the release is split rather than uniformly hawkish. Brent trades at 104.00, up 2.76%, near its 104.40 session high, the 10-year yield is 4.88% and close to its highest since October 2023, the 2-year is 4.48%, and VIX is 16.94, up 2.9%. The observed hold of a session extreme alongside an aligned yields, oil and volatility stack lifts tail from 18 into the watch band, while the softer core and benign claims keep it well below the block threshold.
recommendation: Tail at 20 maps the policy state to WATCH for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD, with pause false and caution true under the fixed repository mapping. The narrow evidence-based danger window runs 12:30-14:30 UTC, covering the post-PPI repricing leg, the 13:30 UTC U.S. cash open and the first full cash hour. That is where an already one-way pre-market tape, a long end near multi-year highs and an oil market near its session high could combine into the kind of shallow-pullback structure that matters for a mean-reversion book. Outside that window the conditional path decays through the U.S. afternoon toward a 10 overnight floor, then drifts back to 18 into the hour before tomorrow's August consumer price release. Stress stays extreme at 85 throughout because the energy-driven inflation impulse, an ECB that raised rates today and a Federal Reserve decision on 16 September are all unresolved. Stress at that level describes the environment; it does not on its own move the mapped state past the block threshold.
headline: NQ holds its 29,216.75 Globex low at 29,235.50 as August PPI splits hot headline against softer core; tail rises to 20 and the mapped state moves to WATCH
body:
The Nasdaq-100 met the August producer price release with the most one-sided pre-market structure of the week. NQ futures were last verified at 29,235.50, down 213.25 points or 0.72%, after opening the Globex session at 29,458.50 and grinding to a low that extended across successive observations from 29,230.00 to 29,227.50 and then 29,216.75. Price sat on that low rather than retracing from it. E-mini S&P 500 futures mirrored the pattern at 7,627.25 against a 7,626.00 session low. Holding a session extreme while the low keeps being extended is the single most relevant observation for a mean-reversion book, and it is why tail moves from the 18 published earlier in this clock-hour into the watch band.

The release itself was not the clean hawkish shock the tape appeared to be positioning for. Headline producer prices rose 0.4% on the month, in line with consensus, and the annual rate accelerated to 5.4% from 4.8%, which two independent sources confirm. But core producer prices rose only 0.2% against a 0.3% consensus, and the annual core rate at 4.6% matched expectations. Initial jobless claims at 206K against 205K expected and continuing claims at 1,774K below forecast add no labour-market shock. The hot half of the print is the energy-driven headline; the rates-relevant core came in softer. That split is why the dominant mode is read as event/whipsaw rather than trend-down, and why tail is lifted only to the bottom of the watch band.

The cross-asset backdrop is coherent, which is what gives the structure weight. Brent crude trades at 104.00, up 2.76% and close to its 104.40 session high, having passed 100 for the first time since July. The move traces to the seventh month of U.S.-Iran conflict, with attacks on shipping in and around the Strait of Hormuz intensifying and Saudi August output reported at its lowest level since 1990. The 10-year Treasury yield is 4.88%, up about four basis points and near its highest since October 2023, with the 2-year at 4.48%; the Federal Reserve's own H.15 release put the 8 September readings at 4.80% and 4.39%, so the long end has extended since. The European Central Bank raised its deposit rate 25 basis points to 2.50% this morning, explicitly citing energy-driven inflation pressure from the Middle East conflict. VIX at 16.94 is up 2.9% but remains at an absolute level that does not describe a disorderly market.

The limitation on this assessment is specific and worth stating plainly. Every quote feed reachable at assessment time was reporting prints from roughly 12:18 to 12:22 UTC, which is before the 12:30 UTC release. The one-way structure described above is therefore genuinely observed, but it is observed into the release rather than after it. No claim is made here about the post-release price path, because none can be verified yet. That is the main reason confidence sits at 84 rather than higher despite the release outcome itself being confirmed from two independent sources.

The forward path treats the 13:30 UTC cash open as the point of maximum conditional risk, since that is where any post-release repricing leg would meet opening-auction flow on a tape that spent the morning on its lows. Conditional tail peaks at 21 in that hour, holds 20 through the first full cash hour, and then decays as the release fades from the tape. Stress remains extreme across the whole window because none of the structural drivers resolve inside it: the oil shock is a live geopolitical process, the August consumer price release follows tomorrow at 12:30 UTC just beyond the end of this window, and the Federal Reserve decides on 16 September with the market pricing a move higher in the policy rate.

lookbackSummary: All 24 clock-hours from 12:00 UTC on 9 September to 11:00 UTC on 10 September carry a published Claude assessment, so every lookback slot is available and none is reconstructed. The window opens on its own high point: tail 20 with the mapped state at WATCH in the 12:00 UTC slot on 9 September, the only watch-band reading inside the lookback. Tail then fell back to 17 and 10 through that U.S. afternoon, ticked to 16 in the 15:00 UTC hour on an event/whipsaw read, and settled into a 13 to 9 band across the U.S. close and the overnight session. The Asian and early European hours of 10 September held a narrow 8 to 11 range with a mixed dominant mode and confidence steady at 87 to 88. The final slot marks the turn: tail 14 at 11:00 UTC with the dominant mode switching to trend-down as the pre-release grind became directional. Stress never left the extreme band across the whole window, ranging from 80 to 83, which is the clearest signal that a difficult high-volatility environment has coexisted with a tail score that stayed below the block threshold for the entire 24 hours. Past assessments are reported as they were published and are not revised using later information.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours are shaped by a producer price release that has just printed and a consumer price release that lands immediately after this window closes. Conditional tail peaks at 21 in the 13:00 UTC slot, where the U.S. cash open sits, holds 20 through the first full cash hour and never approaches the block threshold. It then decays through the U.S. afternoon, ticks back to 16 for the power hour where closing-auction flow can extend a directional day, and reaches a 10 floor across the Asian session. From the European pre-open it drifts back up through 11, 13 and 16 to 18 in the final slot, the hour before the August consumer price index at 12:30 UTC on 11 September. That anticipatory drift deliberately raises stress and lowers confidence more than it raises tail, because hypothetical post-event alignment is not treated as observed structure. Stress runs from 85 in the release hours down to a 75 overnight trough and back to 83 pre-CPI. Confidence falls from 84 to 70 across the window, reflecting how much of the forward path depends on price structure that has not yet formed. Beyond the window, the Federal Reserve decision and press conference on 16 September remain the dominant scheduled risk.
